charts.title: China Revenue by Channel
charts.annotation: OnlineSales and WholesaleRevenue are group-wide, not China-only; RetailStoreRevenueChina and RoboshopRevenueChina are China-specific. Roboshops is unattended vending-machine-style stores, distinct from staffed retail stores.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

channelMix.title: China revenue by channel
channelMix.content:
Pop Mart sells through four China channels: staffed retail stores, online (app, WeChat mini-program, Tmall/other e-commerce), unattended roboshops (vending-machine-style kiosks), and wholesale to third-party distributors.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: retail stores remain the largest China channel (RMB10.1bn of FY2025's RMB20.9bn China revenue) but roboshops are the capital-light format management is scaling fastest (store count below) -- the channel mix is the distribution-efficiency half of the thesis, next to the plush-vs-figures product-mix shift.

What to watch:

  • Roboshop and online revenue growing faster than retail-store revenue (lower fixed cost per RMB of sales)
  • Wholesale share shrinking as the group favours owned channels
  • Note: OnlineSales and WholesaleRevenue are reported group-wide (China + overseas), not China-only, so this chart mixes a China-only pair with a group-wide pair -- read the retail/roboshop lines as the China-specific signal

roboshopCount.title: Roboshop store count
roboshopCount.content:
Count of roboshops (unattended, vending-machine-style kiosks) operating in China at period end -- the physical footprint behind the roboshop revenue line in the channel-mix chart.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: roboshops cost far less to open and staff than a full retail store, so store-count growth here is a cheaper way to add China distribution points than the staffed-store network.

What to watch:

  • Revenue per roboshop (channel revenue above divided by this count) -- rising store count with flat per-store revenue signals saturation
  • Store count growth relative to staffed retail-store growth (not charted here, see StoresChina)

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Pop Mart International Group Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
